ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular iron-core magnetic circuit, with a window in the middle, and coils wound respectively on the left and right vertical side limbs; the two windings are located on opposite vertical limbs. The problem statement gives that the cross-sectional areas of the vertical limbs are both 20 cm², and the cross-sectional areas of the horizontal limbs are both 10 cm². Reasoning: According to the specified method, regard the mutual inductance as proportional to the cross-sectional area of the iron-core limb on which the coupled windings are placed. Originally the windings are on opposite vertical limbs, corresponding to an area of 20 cm²; if they are instead wound on opposite horizontal limbs, the corresponding area becomes 10 cm². Therefore the ratio of new to old mutual inductance is 10/20 = 1/2, so the mutual inductance becomes half of the original.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the transformer core is a rectangular magnetic frame with one winding on each vertical side limb. From the text, note that each vertical limb has cross-sectional area 20 cm², while each horizontal limb has cross-sectional area 10 cm². Treat the original mutual flux linkage as proportional to the area of the limbs on which the coupled windings are placed. If both windings are moved from opposite vertical limbs to opposite horizontal limbs, the relevant cross-sectional area changes from 20 cm² to 10 cm². Therefore the ratio of new to old mutual inductance is 10/20 = 1/2, so the mutual inductance is halved.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the original arrangement has the two coils on the opposite vertical arms of a rectangular iron core. The text gives Av = 20 cm² for vertical arms and Ah = 10 cm² for horizontal arms, with frequency and windings otherwise unchanged. Compare the secondary induced voltage for the same excitation using E = 4.44 f N Φmax. Moving the windings to horizontal arms makes the linked flux capacity proportional to Ah instead of Av. Thus Enew/Eold = Φnew/Φold = Ah/Av = 10/20 = 1/2. Since mutual inductance is proportional to the induced voltage per unit rate of current change, the mutual inductance becomes one-half of its original value.
